questions.text: What specific success metrics should we define for this pilot to measure its effectiveness beyond just tracking functionality?
questions.answer: [synthetic · wind tunnel] For measuring effectiveness beyond functionality, I'd suggest tracking student engagement metrics like daily active users, session duration, and feature adoption rates. We should also collect feedback through quarterly surveys focusing on user satisfaction and perceived value. Financial metrics would be important too - cost per student and any savings generated compared to manual processes.

questions.text: What are the bandwidth constraints we should design for, and what is the minimum acceptable performance on low-bandwidth connections?
questions.answer: [synthetic · wind tunnel] Bandwidth constraints should definitely be considered for our student population. Many students use campus Wi-Fi which can be unreliable in certain areas. We should design for connections as low as 256kbps for basic functionality. Minimum acceptable performance would be load times under 5 seconds for core features on low bandwidth, with graceful degradation options like simplified interfaces when connectivity is poor.

questions.text: What is the exact scope of the manual position updating feature in the admin dashboard, and under what conditions would GPS be expected to fail?
questions.answer: [synthetic · wind tunnel] The manual position updating feature in the admin dashboard allows staff to override GPS coordinates when needed - typically for indoor locations or areas with poor satellite reception. GPS might fail in buildings with thick walls, underground areas, or during extreme weather conditions. The feature would also be used when students report location inaccuracies.

questions.text: What specific Arabic dialect and language requirements should we prioritize for the app's interface?
questions.answer: [synthetic · wind tunnel] For Arabic language requirements, we should focus on Modern Standard Arabic (MSA) for formal communications, but include support for Egyptian Arabic dialect in user-facing features since that's our primary student demographic. The interface should be fully right-to-left with appropriate cultural adaptations for date formats, currency display, and local naming conventions.
